title: Working with LLMs
summary: How large language models produce text (next-token prediction, Transformers, attention), and how to write prompts that reliably get useful answers using the CREF framework and named prompting techniques.
goal: Write a structured prompt with CREF and work out whether a bad answer came from your prompt or from the model's limits.
required: Part I: IBM – Getting Started with Generative AI
Part I: Anthropic – AI Fluency for Students
Part I: Anthropic – AI Capabilities & Limitations
Part I: FreeCodeCamp Python Certification – complete 50 steps
Part II: IBM – Craft Precise Prompts for AI Models
Part II: FreeCodeCamp JavaScript Certification – complete 100 steps

steps.title: Read "What are Large Language Models"
steps.detail: Follow the path from rule-based to retrieval-based to generative chatbots, then how an LLM predicts the next token. Note which models are encoder-only, decoder-only or encoder-decoder, and how Claude, Gemini and ChatGPT compare.
steps.doneWhen: You can explain next-token prediction to a friend in two sentences.

steps.title: Learn CREF and the five bad-prompt patterns
steps.detail: CREF stands for Clarity, Role/Context, Examples, Format. The five failure patterns are too vague, missing context, contradictory, overloaded and assumed knowledge. Study the lecture's "Anatomy of a Good Prompt".
steps.code:
[Role / Persona]
You are a software engineering instructor teaching junior developers.

[Context]
The student just learned about for loops in Python and is now seeing list 
comprehensions for the first time.

[Task]
Explain list comprehensions step by step, starting from the equivalent for loop,
and then showing the compressed syntax.

[Format]
Use a code block for each example. Keep the explanation under 200 words.

[Constraint]
Do not use lambda functions or any concepts beyond basic iteration.
steps.doneWhen: You can take a vague prompt like "Help me with my code" and rewrite it to fix each CREF gap.

steps.title: Run the iterative prompting experiment
steps.detail: Open Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini in three tabs. Work through Scenario 1's six prompts in order in one conversation, then Scenario 2 (Resume Review). After each answer, note what the model assumed and what was missing. The first two prompts are below; the rest are on the page.
steps.code:
Help me plan a birthday party.

Plan a birthday party for my 8-year-old daughter. There will be 15 kids.
Our budget is $200.
steps.doneWhen: You have a short note on which refinement changed the answer most, and which model did best at each stage.

steps.title: Try the four named techniques
steps.detail: Zero-shot (no examples), few-shot (2–3 examples first), chain-of-thought (reason step by step) and role/persona. Try the lecture's chain-of-thought example, then write one of each for something from your own week.
steps.code:
A Django view is returning a 500 error when a POST request comes in but works fine
for GET requests. Think through the most likely causes step by step, then suggest
a debugging strategy.
steps.doneWhen: You've written and tested one prompt for each technique.

steps.title: Diagnose a bad response
steps.detail: Ask "whose fault is it?" A prompt problem (too general, missed the point, inconsistent) is fixed by rewording. A model limit (hallucination, knowledge cutoff, context window, capability ceiling) needs a different approach, like pasting in current docs. If three rewrites fail the same way, it's probably the model.
steps.doneWhen: You can name the four model limitations and what to do about each.

steps.title: Part I: IBM and Anthropic courses
steps.detail: Do IBM's Getting Started with Generative AI, then Anthropic's AI Fluency for Students and AI Capabilities & Limitations. The page warns that AI changes fast, so some course content may be outdated. These aren't tracked in progress.md, so keep your own checklist.
steps.doneWhen: All three courses show as completed in their platforms.

steps.title: Part I: 50 FreeCodeCamp Python steps
steps.detail: Complete 50 steps of the FreeCodeCamp Python certification.
steps.doneWhen: Your FreeCodeCamp progress shows 50 more Python steps done.

steps.title: Part II: precise prompts + 100 JavaScript steps
steps.detail: Do IBM's Craft Precise Prompts for AI Models, then 100 steps of the FreeCodeCamp JavaScript certification. (The page's JavaScript line says "for receiving your Python Certification", which looks like a typo; the link goes to JavaScript.)
steps.doneWhen: The IBM course is complete and FreeCodeCamp shows 100 more JavaScript steps.

concepts.meaning: A model trained on huge amounts of text that writes by predicting the next token over and over.
The model picks the most likely next piece of text, adds it, and repeats.
The model design that lets an LLM weigh every part of the conversation at once when choosing the next token.
Shaping what you give a model, on purpose, so its answers are accurate and in the format you need.
Clarity, Role/Context, Examples, Format: four checks for a good prompt.
Asking with no examples vs. showing 2–3 input → output examples first.
Asking the model to reason step by step before answering, which helps with debugging and math.
A confident, plausible answer that is simply wrong.
The date the model's training data ends; it doesn't know anything newer unless you paste it in.
